findings.message: Approved leave is read with a system job context (`contextFor.job`) and shown to the viewer, so Leave's visibility rule is skipped. 072 reads leave as the viewer and sets `leaveVisible: false` where Leave hides it (utilisation.ts:35, :69). This change adds four more copies that read it as a job: grid-context.ts ("On leave" cells on Team time), anomalies.ts `missingDays` (the approve card's "Check: missing …" leaves out leave days), reminders.ts `dayState` (the remind card says "skipped: on approved leave") and my-days.ts. Fix: read leave through `approvedLeave(tx, viewer, …)` and filter with `leaveVisibleTo`, in one shared helper. Where the viewer can't see a person's leave, show the day as unknown, never as leave. The same applies to `listPeople(tx, job, {})` for departments.
findings.scenario: A PM who can't see Ayesha's leave under Leave's rule opens Team time → her Mon to Wed cells read "On leave" (a sick day is exposed), and remind_missing lists her as "skipped: on approved leave".

findings.message: Round 3 gave remind_weeks and remind_missing a savepoint per person, so one failure fails only that person. The scheduled loops in `remindDaily` and `remindDrafts` were missed: they write every reminder in the service's single transaction. One person's failed insert rolls back the whole entity run. The step retries 3 times, then nobody in the entity is reminded. Fix: wrap each `writeDayReminder` and `recordReminder` in `tx.transaction`, record the failure, and continue. Add a variant test that makes the first person, the last person, and everyone fail.
findings.scenario: A trigger rejects the reminder insert for one user in the LK entity → the 16:00 daily run throws → after the retries, no one in LK gets a reminder that day.

findings.message: `switchedOff` judges a person only by the projects they logged time on in the last 28 days. `expectedIn` also includes people who are only allocated (no entries). Their project switch is never checked, so a PM's switch-off doesn't reach them. Fix: include the person's allocated projects (through the allocations contract) in the projects that `switchedOff` considers.
findings.scenario: Liam is allocated only to FLT and has logged no time. Nimal switches FLT reminders off → the daily run still reminds Liam.

findings.message: `claimChoice` claims every sibling option's key as cancelled and records them as "Not chosen" before the chosen option runs. If the chosen write then fails for good (failed, or the input is refused), nothing was written, but every other option is already closed. The person can't pick the option that would have worked. The UI also keeps the siblings open, because it closes them only on done or cancelled. Fix: on a final failure, release the siblings (or claim them only after the write commits, inside the same keyed run), and test the failure path.
findings.scenario: A choice card has A (fix entry X) and B (fix entry Y). The person confirms A, but entry X changed meanwhile, so A fails → clicking B returns "cancelled", and neither change is made.

findings.message: `shownDays` is computed from `entrySums` over every week in the tenant, before the visibility filter. Weekend columns appear for any viewer whenever anyone logged weekend hours, including people outside the viewer's scope. Fix: compute the days from the visible rows only.
findings.scenario: Liam (AU entity, outside Maya's scope) logs a Saturday → Maya's Team time shows empty Sat and Sun columns, which reveals that someone she can't see worked the weekend.

findings.message: The card re-implements the 24-hour daily cap with its own SQL query, alongside `guardDayTotal`, which the service path uses through `logEntry`. Call `guardDayTotal` (or a shared function) so the card and the service can't disagree.
`decided_by` is parsed into a user id twice: in TypeScript here (`decider`) and in SQL in requests-read.ts (`split_part(regexp_replace…)`). Use one helper.

Published contract types changed: `RequestRef.entryId` and `WeekReminded.weekId` became nullable, and a new event was added. The README still says "Version 1" with no note. The module standard requires a new version and a README note when a contract changes after use.

History hides any user message that starts with "Pinned context:", including one the person actually typed. Mark the injected context block structurally (for example a flag on the block) instead of matching its text.
findings.scenario: The user types "Pinned context: why is this here?" → the message disappears from the reopened conversation.

findings.message: Stale invoice suggestions are withdrawn only inside the `invoiceDrafted` handler, so only when a newer draft replaces the old one. `draftFor` (modules/finance/server/drafts.ts:31-32) can also mark the open draft `superseded` and then return null with no event, when the new amount is 0. That happens when the only approved time for the contract is reopened or sent back. No handler runs, and the old draft's suggestion stays open with its old amount. Fix: withdraw the superseded draft's suggestion where the draft is superseded, with or without a new draft. Either emit an event for the supersede itself, or call the withdrawal from `draftFor`. Add a variant test for the zero-amount reopen.
findings.scenario: Kasun's approved Fleet Tracker hours are the only uninvoiced T&M time on the contract this month. Approving it creates a draft and a suggestion: 'Invoice …, 360 USD'. Reopening it marks that draft superseded, and no new draft is made because the amount is 0, so no `invoiceDrafted` event fires. The inbox still offers 'Invoice …, 360 USD' for a draft that no longer stands.

findings.message: `expectedBy` treats anyone with time or an allocation on a project the viewer manages (`managed.has(id)`) as expected, in any legal entity. The 071 rule for project approvers (`mayFix` / `mayPutOn`: `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId, ...inEntity(entity) })`) limits them to the owner's entity, so this is a second copy of the scope rule and the two disagree. `remind_missing`, `remind_weeks` through `notStartedIn`, Team time's Not started rows and the Not started rows in `get_week_utilisation` all read `expectedBy`, so they reach people the viewer's 071 scope excludes. Fix: in the managed branch, also require `can(v, 'time:approve', { projectId, ...inEntity(entityOf(id)) })`, or reuse the chain or entity check. Add a test with a PM scoped to one entity and an out-of-entity person on the managed project.
findings.scenario: Maya is an Admin scoped to Lumen Labs Lanka and PM of Contoso Portal. Liam, in the Australian entity, logged 3 h on CON on Oct 20. Maya asks to remind everyone with no hours on Oct 22. Liam is on the card and gets reminded, and he shows on her Team time as Not started for week 44. 071 says Maya can't see or act on Liam's time, and the demo doc's E8 says Liam never appears in Maya's reminder cards.
